subject: general
question: Which two elements were put in the same slot by Newland?
solution:
The correct answer is** "Co and Ni".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newland **arranged elements in their increasing order of atomic masses and found that every eighth element had the same properties.
 
• This attempt was the first to assign atomic numbers to each element. 
 
• He gave the** Law of Octaves.**
 
• Newland placed** Cobalt (Co) and Nickel (Ni)** in the same group as they had **similar properties.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Newland's law was the first to be **based on atomic weight.**
 
• In this table, every element did not show similar properties after Calcium.
 
• At that time only** 56 elements **were known.
 
• **Iron **also had similar properties to Nickel and Cobalt but it was placed far more than these two.
